interface.title: Cell Explorer: Streamlit version only (streamlit_version.py); the Voila/Jupyter notebook version was not explored
interface.field: Microscopy / histopathology image analysis (H&E histology, fluorescence cell imaging)
interface.stage_of_work: Looking at images and annotating them: picking a region of interest, enhancing it for display, and recording a description plus processing settings for reproducibility
interface.what_it_is_for: Upload JPG microscopy images and pick one. Each image is resized to 500x500. Crop and zoom on a region with X/Y/Zoom sliders, then adjust contrast, brightness and sharpness. Save the 500x500 result, a free-text description (TXT) and the processing parameters (JSON) on the server. Rename Files then tags all three with a shared suffix so the next image's record does not overwrite them. This tree covers only the Streamlit entry point, not the Voila notebook (image-processing-raw-final.ipynb) that the repository is named after.

data.note: histology-he.jpg (H&E breast tissue) and fluorescence-cells-mitotic.jpg (cells with red nuclei, green microtubules and one mitotic cell) were uploaded through the 'Upload Images' file uploader. cell-brightfield.png was refused with 'Error: image/png files are not allowed.' because only JPG is accepted. All saves write files into the app's working directory on the server. Nothing downloads to the browser (the download list stayed empty), so the saved TXT and JSON could not be read back.

features.name: Slider-driven crop and zoom viewport
features.general: The input image is first stretched to a fixed 500x500 square, ignoring its aspect ratio. Two coordinate sliders pick a centre point on that square and a magnification slider sets the zoom. The fixed-size output window updates straight away, and areas outside the image are padded black.
features.specific: Each upload is resized to 500x500 (streamlit_version.py:30), so the X Coordinate (0–500) and Y Coordinate (0–500) sliders cover the whole image. Zoom (1–10) sets a crop that is resized back to the 500x500 'Processed Image'.
steps: Set Zoom to 1 to see the whole (500x500-resized) field
Find the feature and drag X / Y to centre it
Raise Zoom to magnify (Home/End keys jump to the ends)
Check the black padding where the crop runs past the image edge and move X/Y back inside
serves_tasks: Change magnification to see the whole field or fine detail
Centre the view on a cell or feature of interest

features.name: Live image enhancement sliders
features.general: Adjust contrast, brightness and sharpness with sliders and see the preview change live; extreme values show the limits (contrast 0 gives flat grey, sharpness 0 softens)
features.specific: PIL-style ImageEnhance sliders Contrast (0–5), Brightness (0–5) and Sharpness (0–2), applied to the cropped Processed Image
steps: Raise Contrast to separate nuclei from stroma or background
Lower or raise Brightness to suit a bright H&E or dim fluorescence image
Raise Sharpness to crisp up edges, or lower it to smooth
Check the preview, and the fullscreen view if needed
serves_tasks: Increase contrast and tune brightness and sharpness

features.name: Multi-file upload with index selector
features.general: Load several images at once (type-checked), switch between them with a dropdown, and add or remove files; the list re-indexes and settings carry over to the next image
features.specific: 'Upload Images' file_uploader (JPG only, 200MB per file) with 'Select Image' dropdown listing indices 0..n-1
steps: Upload one or more JPGs (a PNG is refused with an error chip)
Pick an image index in Select Image
Remove a file chip (indices shift down)
Add a file with + (it goes at the end)
serves_tasks: Load one or more images into the tool
Choose which loaded image to work on next

features.name: Reproducibility record: processed image + description + parameter JSON, archived per image
features.general: Save the processed view, a free-text annotation and the exact processing settings as side-by-side files, each with a confirmation message. Then tag all three with a shared suffix so each image's record is kept apart and can be reproduced and reused.
features.specific: The Save Image checkbox is a live toggle: while ticked, it re-saves image-processed.jpg on every slider or image change. The 'Describe the image' text area with Save Description writes saved_image_description.txt, and Save Image Parameters writes saved_image_parameters.json. Rename Files then renames all three with the same random suffix (0–99) so the next record does not overwrite them.
steps: Tick Save Image (while ticked, every change re-saves image-processed.jpg)
Type a description of the feature
Press Rename Files to archive the three files before switching to the next image
serves_tasks: Write and save a free-text description of what is seen
Record the exact processing settings for reproducibility
Archive the current record under a shared unique tag so the next save does not overwrite it

They are written on the server, nothing downloads to the browser, and I had no shell. So the JSON content and the 500x500 size could not be confirmed beyond the fullscreen preview.

The app shows only 'Files renamed successfully' after Rename Files. The new names (img_processed<N>.jpg, saved_image_parameters<N>.json, saved_image_description<N>.txt) come from the code and were not seen on disk.

Rename Files pressed before all three files exist does nothing visible. In the replay, an accidental click made before the parameters JSON was saved showed no message, and the code suggests it fails or errors. Save all three files first.

Records are kept apart only by Rename Files' random suffix from 0 to 99, so two records can collide. Until Rename is pressed, the fixed file names mean saving a second image overwrites the first. With Save Image ticked, image-processed.jpg is also overwritten whenever a slider or the selected image changes.
Every image is stretched to 500x500 before cropping, so non-square images are distorted in the output. The X/Y sliders do cover the whole image.
